record.paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
record.original_question: For a rotationally scalar nuclear Hamiltonian, the energy minimization can be restricted to scalar many-body density operators, so the associated one-body density is a radial monopole profile ρ0(r) and the resulting scalar functional is F0[ρ0]. What features of such radial density profiles determine whether the underlying nucleus is deformed, and can one formulate precise criteria, possibly using profile slopes at the nuclear surface or moments of the profiles, that distinguish spherical from deformed nuclei, hard from soft nuclei, and identify triaxial or halo nuclei?

evidence.quote: Since the energy minimization occurs within a subspace of scalar density operators, the corresponding one-body densities ρ(~r) are just radial profiles, ρ0(r). The final result is a scalar functional, F0[ρ0]. Hence an open problem : for such monopolar profiles ρ0, what is the signature for deformation? It is likely that the slope of ρ0 at the nuclear surface will be weaker for deformed nuclei than for spherical ones, but precise criteria distinguishing hard from soft nuclei are desirable, not to mention criteria identifying triaxial nuclei, halo nuclei, etc. Can one use properties of moments of the profiles?

artifact.status_search_result: The problem of identifying deformation signatures purely from the monopole/radial density profile in scalar nuclear DFT remains a recognized open problem in nuclear density functional theory, with no general criteria established. While studies have related radial moments and surface diffuseness to deformation, no precise mathematical criteria distinguishing spherical, deformed, soft/hard, triaxial, and halo nuclei from ρ₀ alone have been demonstrated. No published resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the question of signatures for deformation in monopolar radial profiles ρ₀ as an open problem in nuclear DFT.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly listed as open in the nuclear DFT open-problems literature.
